newsitem.title: UK: Russia slides, rest of emerging debt rests.
newsitem.headline: Russia slides, rest of emerging debt rests.

text.p: Emerging debt hardly stirred on Wednesday in the wake of the rise in U.S. interest rates.
Traders said Latin American debt was almost completely unchanged from the New York close, though the tone was a touch firmer in line with a slight uptick this morning in U.S. Treasuries.
However, Russia took an early knock, largely on nervousness ahead of a general strike planned for Thursday.
"In our market, Russia is the only thing really trading," one U.S. bank trader said.

Dollar Vneshekonombank debt RUVNUSLNS=RR was bid 3/4 of a point lower, slipping below 80 cents in the dollar for the first time since the beginning of the month, and compared to a peak of 87 cents in late February.
The trader said some investors were put off by Thursday's planned protest in Russia.

Trade unions have predicted that up to 20 million people will strike or join demonstrations to protest massive arrears in wages to workers, owed nearly $9 billion in back wages with many having not been paid for months.
President Boris Yeltsin met his three most senior ministers on Wednesday in the search for how to tackle the country's mass of economic problems.
Traders said the market as a whole, almost paralysed in the run-up to the U.S. interest rate rise, is likely to remain subdued until after the Easter holidays.
